newsitem.title: JAPAN: Crudes dip on Iraqi oil exports, Gulf crudes quiet.
newsitem.headline: Crudes dip on Iraqi oil exports, Gulf crudes quiet.

text.p: Crude oil prices remained soft in Asia on Tuesday, due mainly to U.N. approval of limited Iraqi crude oil exports, while Gulf crudes were mainly quiet in the wet market, traders said.
U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali gave final clearance on Monday for the resumption of Iraqi oil sales under an oil-for-food accord.
"Market sentiment is a bit weaker on that news," a broker said.
January cash Brent was notionally assessed at $23.90/24.00, compared with late-U.S. trading levels of $24.05/24.15.
The Brent/Dubai spread for February was assessed at $1.85/1.92, similar to late-U.S. trading levels of $1.88/1.93.

A March/April Dubai changed hands at 57 cents, while an April/May Dubai switched hands at 51 cents. The seller was the same trader in both cases. A February/March Dubai was exchanged at 59 cents between traders.

In the wet market, 600,000 barrels of Tapis for January loading were sold by a producer to Thailand at market quotes plus $1. The seller had one more January Tapis cargo available that it said it was offering at a premium of $1.10. It said China and one other trader were showing buying interest.
